newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas in talks to buy Ansett NZ - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas in talks to buy Ansett NZ - paper.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd is holding takeover discussions with Ansett New Zealand, which is now wholly owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Friday.
"It is understood Qantas management is keen to make its move well before the end of the year," the Sydney Morning Herald said.
The report did not include any direct sourcing.

"If News is not prepared to sell Ansett New Zealand, Qantas will pursue one of the other options," the newspaper said, referring to Qantas either starting up its own operation in New Zealand or franchising other parties to use Qantas' name.
Qantas sold its 19.4 percent stake in Air New Zealand Ltd, Ansett New Zealand's main competitor, on Wednesday for a profit of A$99 million.
Qantas originally bought the stake as part of a plan to form a strategic alliance, but the stake then became a defensive stake as the prospect of an alliance faded.
Relations between Qantas and Air New Zealand soured further last year when Air New Zealand bought half of Ansett Australia, Qantas' major domestic competitor.

News Corp, which owns the other half of Ansett, bought all of Ansett New Zealand last year to satisfy the New Zealand Commerce Commission's concerns about a lessening of competition if Air New Zealand owned half of its major competitor.
The Sydney Morning Herald reported Qantas managing director James Strong declined to comment on Qantas' exact plans in New Zealand.
But Strong said Qantas was looking at its options in New Zealand.
"Obviously we do have to consider the New Zealand situation and we have been for some time," Strong was quoted as saying.
"Any question whether we would go into New Zealand is completely separater from the share sale. The sale does not trigger an urgency," Strong said.
